about: Annotation spec for the Phase 3 screen-design frames. Coordinates are in screenshot pixels (desktop 1440x900, phone 390x844). kind: ui (gold), ai (cyan), issue (red, only for issues confirmed in testing).

notes.text: One call to action: press Enter or click to start. Keyboard, mouse and touch are all named.
Sign in is optional. Guests save on this device, as the top bar says.

frames.title: Title menu
frames.ai: Rival status chip: checking, online (with model name) or offline (with Connect)

notes.text: New game is the highlighted primary action. Every entry has a one-line explanation (T1).
Continue explains why it is unavailable: "No voyage saved yet".
The AI rival's status is visible before play, so a missing model is never a surprise mid-game (T4).
Voice and sound toggles on the first screen, without opening Settings.
AI Lab: watch the rival's decision pipeline without affecting the campaign.

frames.title: Prologue
frames.ai: Bard voice (Kokoro-82M) reads each card aloud

notes.text: Two short cards set the story. Large type, one idea per card.
Progress dots show how many cards remain.
States that the bard is reading and where to mute the voice.
Escape returns to the menu. The prologue can also be skipped to the voyage map.

frames.title: Trial selection
frames.ai: Per-trial note on the AI technique the rival uses at each difficulty

notes.text: Eight numbered cards in voyage order. The selected trial has a gold outline.
Switch between the trial gallery and the illustrated voyage chart.
The side briefing previews the objective before the player commits.
Explains how the rival behaves on Medium and Hard, in plain words (transparency for Rosa).
The current island is ringed, and the dashed route shows the voyage order from Troy to Ithaca.
The same AI technique note as the gallery, beside the chart.
Difficulty can also be chosen here.
Approach island opens the briefing.
Pilot: some island labels overlap the "wine-dark sea" caption.
Locked, open and cleared islands differ by icon and label, not colour alone.

frames.title: Briefing: the rival is preparing (states 1-2 of 5: initial and loading)
frames.ai: A1 loading: the model reads recent attempts and chooses a strategy (about 15 s on a CPU laptop)

notes.text: Says what the model is doing ("is studying you"), names the model, says whether it is a first meeting, and counts the elapsed seconds.
Cancel preparation: the player is never stuck waiting.
Start says "Waiting for your rival" and is disabled until a plan is ready.
The objective and controls can be read while the model works, so the wait is useful.

frames.title: Briefing: slow response while asking again (state 2 of 5: loading)
frames.ai: Loading during a slow response. Mock AI service in mode slow (12 s, just above the slowest strategy measured in the Phase 2 spike, 11.6 s)

notes.text: Elapsed seconds instead of a fake percentage: the model's time varies, so the bar only shows activity.
Cyan scanning bar: cyan is used only for AI activity.
While a new strategy loads, the previous one is one click away (undo), so a slow model never blocks play.
Captured in the real interface with the mock AI service answering, so the model is named "mock-ai (test mode)".

frames.title: Briefing: strategy ready (state 3 of 5: success)
frames.ai: A1 success: named strategy, who chose it, description and taunt

notes.text: The objective comes first, in plain words.
Difficulty with a plain-language note. Pilot: it defaults to Medium, which new players may not notice.
Strategy name and "Strategy chosen by qwen3:4b-instruct": the AI's decision is labelled as the AI's (T2).
Model-written taunt, with Hear it to play it in the rival's voice.
The rival status chip stays visible on every menu screen.

frames.title: Briefing: another strategy, with undo (user control)
frames.flow: F3 Prepare the rival (A1 success, regenerate and undo)
frames.ai: User control: the player asked for another strategy (Counter-gusts became Gentle breeze) and can undo. Mock AI service in mode success

notes.text: The new strategy, and who chose it: "Strategy chosen by" the model.
Regenerate: Ask for another strategy.
Undo: back to the strategy the player had before. Pressing it again swaps back.
The start button repeats the chosen strategy, so the player knows what they are accepting.
Edit is not offered by design: the strategy is the opponent's move. Changing difficulty asks for a new one.

frames.title: Briefing: controls and start
frames.ai: User control over the AI result: regenerate, start, or practise

notes.text: Ask for another strategy: regenerate the AI result.
Start repeats difficulty and plan and says it counts toward the voyage. Enter is the shortcut.
Short practice: same rival and strategy, nothing saved.
"How does the AI rival work?" says what the model decides and what the game always owns (collisions, scoring, progress).
Explains Escape, F3 and F before the full-screen stage opens.

frames.title: Briefing: AI error (state 5 of 5)
frames.flow: F4 Recover from a failed AI plan (A1 error)
frames.ai: Error: the strategy request failed. Triggered with the mock AI service (mode error-once), which is how Task 4 of the test reaches it

notes.text: A plain message with no error codes, in the red error style.
One clear recovery action, "Prepare the rival again", plus the reassurance "Nothing about your voyage changes".
Start stays disabled. Pilot: its label "The model is choosing a strategy" is wrong while nothing is being prepared.

frames.title: Briefing: no AI rival connected (initial state without a model)
frames.ai: Model service unreachable: play is blocked until a model is connected
frames.simulated: the status check reported the model as unreachable (the mock AI service's offline mode produces the same screen)

notes.text: The header chip turns to "AI rival offline", with Connect.
Names the exact problem and the next step: open Ollama, then check again.
Three ways to connect: this computer, Google Colab, or an online account.
Check again sits below the fold. The game also re-checks every 15 seconds (T4).

frames.title: Briefing: low-confidence result (state 4 of 5)
frames.flow: F4 Recover from a failed AI plan (A1 uncertain)
frames.ai: Low-confidence: the model returned a strategy that failed the game's checks, so it was set aside. Triggered with the mock AI service (mode uncertain-once) after the player asked for another strategy

notes.text: Amber, not red: the AI produced an answer, but the game could not trust it.
Explains the check in plain words. Large language models give no reliable confidence number, so none is invented.
Ask for another strategy: the user regenerates the result. The rejected plan is never used.
Undo: Keep the previous strategy returns to the plan the player had before asking again.
Pilot issue 11: the disabled start button still says "The model is choosing a strategy" while nothing is being prepared.
New in Phase 3: before this, an unverifiable plan looked identical to a connection error.

frames.title: Lotus-Eaters: playing
frames.ai: The chosen strategy runs locally every frame. Commentary lines are written by the model during play

notes.text: Odysseus' portrait and lives, top left.
Score, difficulty, time and pause, top right.
Objective and progress counters stay in view.
Rival card: plan name and current behaviour. Pilot: the plan name and the live line can disagree.
Live from the voyage: the bard's and rival's lines appear here and are spoken.
On-screen direction buttons for mouse and touch players.
Tactical cue strip with the current instruction.
States exactly what is paused: both rivals and every clock.
Resume has a 3-second countdown, so the player is not hit on return. Esc shortcut.
Restart keeps the same rival strategy.
Settings are reachable mid-play.
Return to map warns that the attempt will not be saved.

frames.title: Cyclops' Cave briefing
frames.ai: A1 success for Polyphemus

notes.text: Same briefing layout for every trial, so learning carries over. The cave adds an Original cave tactics practice.

frames.title: Cyclops' Cave: AI Insights
frames.ai: Explainable AI overlay: state, algorithm, chosen action and a grounded reason

notes.text: Mode chips: Immersive, AI Insights, AI Lab. F3 cycles them.
State, algorithm, chosen action, target lane, forecast probability and time until the attack.
"Why?" gives the grounded reason, including the guarantee that an action-free escape lane stays open (T3).
The danger cue is red and in words: "Boulder locked, Centre. Step aside before it lands."
The 76% is a real Markov-model forecast of the player's lane, not an invented confidence. Cyan is used only for AI information.

frames.title: Cyclops' Cave: AI Insights before the first decision (state 1 of 5: empty)
frames.ai: Empty state of the explainable AI panel: the rival is observing and has committed to nothing yet

notes.text: State: Observing. The panel says what the rival is doing even before it acts.
"No committed action": an honest empty state, not a blank box or a made-up reason.
AI Insights is on by default in this encounter. F3 cycles Immersive, AI Insights and AI Lab.
Live bard commentary. In this capture the line comes from the mock AI service.

frames.title: Cyclops' Cave: AI Lab panel
frames.ai: Full decision pipeline: perception, memory, evaluation, decision, execution, result

notes.text: Perception: exactly what the opponent can observe right now.
Memory: what it has recorded about the player's habits (lane dwell, preferred lane).
A withheld option is shown dimmed, with its fairness reason (no action-free escape lane).
Every candidate action with its computed score. The chosen one is highlighted.
The forecast is also drawn in the scene over the targeted lane.
The play area shrinks to make room and returns to full width when the panel is collapsed.
Immersive hides the inspector. Fair attack warnings (the locked-lane stripe and countdown) always stay, because they are gameplay information, not AI debugging.

frames.title: Result: trial failed
frames.ai: Model-written rival line reacting to the attempt

notes.text: Clear outcome, with a specific tip: "Watch the locked lane and move early".
The rival reacts to this attempt in a line written by the model.
Score, time and difficulty.
Retry, Change difficulty, World map and an accessibility Assisted passage sit below.

frames.title: Settings
frames.ai: Which model plans the rivals and which voices the commentary

notes.text: Names the models in use for planning, commentary and voice.
Check connection again, with the reminder that every encounter needs a model.
Live AI commentary on or off.
Spoken voice on or off, separately from commentary.
Voice volume and a voice test.

frames.title: How to play
frames.ai: Explains the AI rival in one sentence

notes.text: "Face a thinking rival": the model reads your attempts and plans the rival, then comments live.
The medal rules are stated exactly.
Controls for all eight trials on one page.

frames.title: AI Lab (professor mode)
frames.ai: Compare the rival across difficulties with the same layout

notes.text: States that lab runs never touch campaign progress.
Choose any of the eight encounters.
Choose a difficulty.
Seeded comparison keeps the layout fixed, so any difference comes from the opponent.
Says the inspector never changes how the opponent plays.
When accounts are not configured, says so and offers play on this device.
"Keep playing on this device" is always available.
Email/password and Google sign-in sync saves through MongoDB when the server is configured.
The AI rival status gets its own full-width row at the top.
Voice and sound toggles follow directly below.
The menu stacks into one column, and every entry keeps its one-line explanation.
"No account needed. Your voyage saves as you play."
Story and objective come first, in large type.
Controls are explained in words, including touch.
Pilot: on a phone the rival's strategy panel and the start button are several screens further down.
Portrait, then score, time and pause: the same HUD order as desktop.
Large on-screen direction buttons for touch.
Progress (crew aboard) and the current instruction sit directly under the maze.
Objective and counters follow below.

frames.title: Cyclops' Cave with AI Insights (phone)
frames.ai: Insights panel below the play area

notes.text: Mode chips: Immersive, AI Insights, AI Lab.
Touch controls: lane left and right, Jump, Slide.
The locked-lane warning is in words as well as colour.
Pilot: the Insights panel sits below the play area on a phone, so it cannot be read while dodging.
